newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Moody's says Lithuania moving in right direction.
newsitem.headline: Moody's says Lithuania moving in right direction.

text.p: U.S. credit ratings agency Moody's said on Tuesday that Lithuania was moving in the right direction and carrying out the necessary policies.

"I think they are moving in the right direction and carrying out the right policies in terms of privatisation and privatisation regulations," Moody's economist Sosi Vartanesyan told Reuters by telephone from New York.

Moody's reviews ratings periodically, but constantly monitors economies of countries they have rated for new developments, Vartanesyan said. She could not say when Lithuania's rating would be looked at again.
Lithuania was the first of the former Soviet republics to receive a rating. Moody's in September assigned a Ba2 rating to Lithuania's foreign currency debt and a Ba3 to the country's bank deposits.
It also received a BB+ credit rating from European credit ratings agency IBCA this year.
